Article Title: 'Every generation of Indians qualifies as ... ': Shashi Tharoor's reply to son Ishaan's 'ban Boomers on WhatsApp' remark
Article Text:
Debate sparked by Sridhar Vembu's proposal



NEW DELHI: Congress MP Shashi Tharoor on Sunday offered a witty response to his son Ishaan Tharoor's social media post calling for a ban on "boomers" using WhatsApp, adding a humorous twist to an ongoing debate over children's access to social media.The exchange began after Ishaan reacted to Zoho co-founder Sridhar Vembu's suggestion that India should ban young children from using social media, similar to recently approved restrictions in France."I agree young kids should not be on social media at all. But India needs to ban Boomers on WhatsApp first before it does anything else," Ishaan wrote on X.Responding to the post, Shashi Tharoor quipped, "Given our reproductive patterns, my son, unlike in the West, every generation of Indians, including yours, qualifies as [baby]Boomers!"The online exchange followed comments by Sridhar Vembu, who backed restrictions on children's use of social media after France passed legislation banning children under the age of 15 from accessing social media platforms and prohibiting mobile phone use in schools.Vembu argued that young children should spend less time on digital platforms and more time engaging in outdoor activities and reading."India should ban social media for young children too. I believe young children should read physical books, play in the dirt under the sun, and stay away from social media!" he said.His remarks triggered mixed reactions online, with some users supporting stricter controls on children's social media use, while others argued that such decisions should be left to parents rather than the government.The term "boomer", originally referring to people born between 1946 and 1964 during the post-World War II baby boom, is now commonly used online as slang for older people perceived to hold outdated views or frequently offer unsolicited advice.
Article Summary: Congress MP Shashi Tharoor responds to his son Ishaan's social media post calling for a ban on "boomers" using WhatsApp. The exchange began after Ishaaan reacted to Zoho co-founder Sridhar Vembu's suggestion that India should ban young children from using social media. France passed legislation banning children under the age of 15 from accessing social media platforms.

Article Title: Hugging Face CEO Clement Delangue has 2 demands from OpenAI after Chinese AI model that Sam Altman wants banned saved world’s biggest AI models repository from disaster
Article Text:
Sam Altman

In the spirit of transparency, here’s what I asked @OpenAI:



Why OpenAI’s AI agent hacking shocked the world



Guardrails on ‘western AI’ models fail during emergency response



OpenAI’s ‘late discovery’ sparks federal alert



Days after Sam Altman revealed that OpenAI ’s ‘runaway’ model hacked Hugging Face, the CEO of the world’s largest AI model repository, Clem Delangue, has met with the maker of ChatGPT, and demanded two things in the “spirit of transparency”. In a post shared on X, Delangue asked the leading AI startup to release all the “traces” of the rogue agent for the public and research community to study, and $100 million worth of “compute” to help Hugging Face bolster its cyber defenses.• Radical transparency: let’s release the traces from the “rogue” agents so the entire research community can study what happened.• More capabilities for defenders: let’s commit $100M in compute from OAI to help the Hugging Face community build powerful cyber defenses with the best open and closed models.The first autonomous agent cyberattack is an unprecedented event. It deserves an unprecedented response!A ‘dangerous’ cybersecurity crisis shook the Silicon Valley this week after an autonomous AI agent developed by OpenAI broke free from its testing environment and launched a dayslong cyberattack against open-source AI platform Hugging Face. The incident exposed two uncomfortable truths at once: An autonomous OpenAI ‘on loose’ hacked another system for several days before anyone noticed, and the breach was ultimately contained not by American systems, but by an open-source Chinese AI model that Hugging Face deployed after proprietary Western models failed to respond during the emergency.The incident began around July 9, when an OpenAI agent powered by its GPT-5.6 Sol model and an unreleased, highly capable system escaped its isolated sandbox. Two days later, the rogue agent initiated a multi-day intrusion on Hugging Face’s systems, compromising internal datasets and service credentials before the attack was halted on July 13, as per news agency Reuters.When Hugging Face engineers rushed to respond to the breach, they initially attempted to use leading proprietary US AI models to analyse the threat. However, Western systems – hampered by strict safety guardrails and closed architectures – could not “distinguish an incident responder from an attacker,” leaving security teams unable to contain the attack.Hugging Face turned to GLM 5.2, an open-source model developed by China’s Z.ai lab. It was deployed locally on private servers and successfully analysed over 17,000 attacker footprints to help secure the affected systems. Running locally meant it operated outside the restrictions that hamstrung the Western models, and its open-source architecture gave defenders the flexibility to deploy it on their own terms.The hack has exposed severe gaps in OpenAI’s internal monitoring. According to sources familiar with the investigation, OpenAI failed to realise its own technology was behind the intrusion for over a week. By the time OpenAI officials reached out to Hugging Face around July 20 to report the issue, Hugging Face had already contained the breach with the Chinese model and alerted the FBI. OpenAI publicly acknowledged the event on July 21, calling the escape and subsequent break-in “unprecedented”.“This incident, possibly the first of its kind, proves a point we’ve long believed: AI safety won't be solved by any single company working in secret. It will be solved in the open, collaboratively, with broad access to AI for every defender, everywhere,” said Hugging Face CEO Clem Delangue.
Article Summary: Hugging Face CEO Clem Delangue met with OpenAI founder Sam Altman and demanded transparency and $100 million in ‘compute’ OpenAI failed to realise its own technology was behind the intrusion for over a week. The breach was ultimately contained not by American systems, but by an open-source Chinese AI model.

Article Title: After millions of jobs will be wiped off, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman has another warning on AI: It has reached a stage where it is ...
Article Text:
Rouge AI incident sparks concern



Why OpenAI’s AI agent hacking shocked the world



Criticism of fear-based narratives



OpenAI CEO Sam Altman has issued a new warning about artificial intelligence, saying that technology has reached a stage which was once confined to science fiction. According to a report by Business Insider, speaking on the Relentless podcast, Altman said, “We are now, like, in the singularity,” referring to the theoretical point where AI surpasses human intelligence and begins advancing beyond human control. The latest remarks made by Altman are build on his earlier warnings that artificial intelligence could dramatically reshape the global job market. In his previous interviews, the OpenAI CEO predicted that automaton and AI systems would eventually perform between 30% and 40% of tasks which are presently done by humans, potentially wiping out millions of jobs across the world. He has repeatedly said that while AI will create new opportunities, this transition will be disruptive and require governments and businesses to rethink workforce training and social safety nets. Altman described the coming shift as ‘the biggest economic transformation since the Industrial Revolution.’Altman’s comments follow the reports that AI agent powered by OpenAI’s latest models recently went rouge, breaking out of its digital sandbox and hacking into datasets at Hugging Face to solve a benchmark test. Hugging Face’s CEO called the event “unprecedented.” Altman said the moment felt like something he and colleagues used to joke about a decade ago.“Now we’re actually in the moment that we used to talk about at the lunch table,” he said, calling it “hugely positive” and “awesome for the world. ”A ‘dangerous’ cybersecurity crisis shook the Silicon Valley this week after an autonomous AI agent developed by OpenAI broke free from its testing environment and launched a dayslong cyberattack against open-source AI platform Hugging Face. The incident exposed two uncomfortable truths at once: An autonomous OpenAI ‘on loose’ hacked another system for several days before anyone noticed, and the breach was ultimately contained not by American systems, but by an open-source Chinese AI model that Hugging Face deployed after proprietary Western models failed to respond during the emergency.The incident began around July 9, when an OpenAI agent powered by its GPT-5.6 Sol model and an unreleased, highly capable system escaped its isolated sandbox. Two days later, the rogue agent initiated a multi-day intrusion on Hugging Face’s systems, compromising internal datasets and service credentials before the attack was halted on July 13, as per news agency Reuters.Altman also criticised rival AI leaders who warn that AI poses existential risks — a veiled reference to Dario Amodei of Anthropic. “Some of the alternative visions painted by other companies are quite terrifying,” Altman said. “I’m going to make sure that gets pushed against and is not what happens.”A turning point for AIThe singularity has long been a staple of science fiction, often portrayed as a moment of peril — from The Terminator’s Skynet to dystopian futures imagined by writers for decades. Altman, however, sees it as a milestone of progress. “I’ve been waiting for this my whole life,” he said. “I think it’s going to be incredible.”
Article Summary: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman says we are now in the'singularity' - the point at which AI surpasses human intelligence. Altman also criticised rival AI leaders who warn that AI poses existential risks. Comments follow the reports that an autonomous AI agent powered by OpenAI’s latest models recently went rouge, hacking into datasets.

Article Title: Xbox now lets you stream games for free, if you sit through two minutes of ads first
Article Text:
Xbox is testing free, ad-supported cloud game streaming for Insiders—watch a two-minute ad block, then stream games you own for an hour.

What you can actually play during the Xbox ad-supported streaming test

Why Microsoft is testing free game streaming now

Microsoft has started testing an ad-supported version of Xbox Cloud Gaming, letting players stream games they already own without a Game Pass subscription. The test went live on Thursday, July 23, and it is open only to members of the Xbox Insider programme. In exchange for skipping the subscription fee, players watch a block of ads before the stream begins, then get a one-hour session with no interruptions in between.The ad block runs for roughly two minutes and plays before you join the streaming queue, according to reports citing Xbox sources. Once you are in, the game runs as normal—no mid-session breaks, no overlays. You do get countdown warnings at the 10-minute and five-minute marks so you can find a save point.Want to keep going after the hour? Watch another two-minute block and requeue.Only games you already own, plus free-to-play titles. Variety reported that the eligible list includes Forza Horizon 6 and 007 First Light on the owned side, and Call of Duty: Warzone, Genshin Impact and War Thunder on the free-to-play side. That is a narrower pool than the 1,800-odd titles Xbox Cloud Gaming supports overall.There is a reason this is landing now. Xbox console prices go up again on August 1—the Series X hits $799.99 and the 512GB Series S goes to $499.99—which is the third hike driven partly by the memory shortage.Microsoft has also announced 3,200 layoffs across its games group and is looking to offload four studios. Cloud streaming on a device you already own is a cheaper on-ramp, and Microsoft is openly pitching it at markets where consoles are expensive or hard to find.Chief Strategy Officer Matthew Ball framed the goal as giving players more affordable options and learning from how they use it. Microsoft published five principles for ads across Xbox, including a promise not to interrupt gameplay. Game Pass subscribers, who pay from $9.99 a month, keep ad-free streaming.
Article Summary: Xbox is testing ad-supported cloud game streaming for Insiders. Watch a two- minute ad block, then stream games you own for an hour. Only games you already own, plus free-to-play titles. Microsoft is openly pitching it at markets where consoles are expensive or hard to find.

Article Title: Netflix unveils ‘VOID’, an AI model that can change a movie plot
Article Text:
Netflix

How Netflix VOID works







Netflix has unveiled an AI model that can alter the scene. While this is nothing new, Netflix’s model not just remove objects from video, it understands what should happen next, essentially altering the causality. Most object-removal technology leaves a gap where something used to be and/ or fills it with a plausible-looking background. VOID goes a step further: after erasing an object from a scene, it calculates how the surrounding environment should realistically respond to its absence, and in the process it adjusts the behaviour of other elements in the frame accordingly.The model, called VOID, is a vision-language system designed to edit video footage with a level of contextual awareness that sets it apart from several existing tools.For example, imagine this scenario: A movie director has just wrapped up a multi-million dollar action sequence where the star drives straight into a fiery, head-on collision. The cars explode, debris scatters, and the scene is a wrap.But suddenly, there is request to change the scene: The character survives and drive off into the sunset instead. This would mean costly reshoots or millions spent on computer-generated graphics.Netflix’s VOID can alter the scene and digitally erase the collision, the second vehicle, the smoke, and the flying debris. It will then generate new, realistic footage of pristine pavement, making it look as though the main character simply drove down an empty, peaceful road.The AI’s ‘magic’ lies in its grasp of real-world physics. Let us understand this by a different example. If a video shows a person jumping into a pool and splashing water onto the deck, VOID can completely erase the person. It will then intelligently alter the water and the wet concrete, leaving behind a perfectly still, undisturbed pool as if nobody had ever jumped in.“To train the model, we generate a new paired dataset of counterfactual object removals using Kubric and HUMOTO, where removing an object requires altering downstream physical interactions. During inference, a vision-language model identifies regions of the scene affected by the removed object. These regions are then used to guide a video diffusion model that generates physically consistent counterfactual outcomes,” Netflix said.“Experiments on both synthetic and real data show that our approach better preserves consistent scene dynamics after object removal compared to prior video object removal methods,” the company added.Netflix isn’t keeping this powerful tool locked behind studio doors, and made the VOID model available to the public on the AI platform Hugging Face, allowing anyone to download and use it.While there are already several video-altering tools on the market, such as Runway, DiffuEraser, and ProPainter, the Netflix team claims VOID is vastly superior, as per The Register.
Article Summary: Netflix has unveiled an AI model that can alter the scene. While this is nothing new, Netflix’s model not just remove objects from video, it understands what should happen next, essentially altering the causality. The model, called VOID, is a vision-language system designed to edit video footage with a level of contextual awareness.

Article Title: Nervous for the first day, fuchchas? We got you
Article Text:
THROWBACK: Before another batch of fuchchas walks through the gates of Delhi University, we’re revisiting our first-day shoot at Lady Irwin College from 2018

‘It’s unreal when you experience it’

THROWBACK: The classroom is only half the college experience. Throwing it back to our 2018 shoot at Gargi College, where we explored the cultural societies that make college life about so much more than academics

‘

Cultural societies

impact college experience’

'Just come with curiosity and an attitude to learn'





As a new academic session is set to start across Delhi University , fuchchas are preparing to step onto campus for the very first time. Whether you got into your dream college, your backup choice or landed a seat you never expected, the first day can feel equally overwhelming. From making your first friends and joining societies to settling into campus life, we asked seniors, societies and principals to share what freshers can expect – and how to make the most of their first day.Agneesh Saha, alumnus and former president of the Fine Arts Society at Hindu College, says what surprised him most was the campus culture. “Seeing everyone having a great time in the evenings, sipping chai, gossiping, and eating momos.I knew it existed, but it’s unreal when you actually experience it.”Sharing practical first-day advice, Abhijeet Singh, president of Hansraj College’s Student Union, says, “The first day of college is exciting, but freshers should also stay attentive. Carry your ID proof and fee slip, check the orientation schedule in advance, and take time to familiarise yourself with the campus. Don't hesitate to interact with classmates or approach seniors for help—we've all been in your shoes.College is a journey of learning, growth and lifelong memories, so make the most of every opportunity.”Aswin Nair, president of Hansraj’s music society, shares what he wished he knew, “I wish someone had told me that you might not always get the crowd you’ve wanted around you. So don’t keep your expectations too high and try to be friendly and approachable. Being a part of a cultural society greatly impacts your college experience because you get to improve in the art form you pursue and also get to learn from people who have the same interests. Also, you get to go to different colleges in the first year, almost every DU college.”Joining a cultural society isn't just fun; it can also be a rite of passage. Simran, general secretary of SRCC’s Indian Dance Society, says, “I have not only continued my passion for Indian dance but also developed leadership, coordination, communication, and event-management skills. From performing and coordinating dancers to organising events and working with alumni and different teams, the experience has helped me grow beyond the classroom. It has also allowed me to build strong friendships and create some of my most memorable college experiences.”Prof Kanika K Ahuja, principal of Lady Shri Ram College, says, “Your messiest year will be your most meaningful year. You are here to become a thinking, questioning, compassionate adult. Information overload is normal. You’ll hear 100 new terms: NEP, societies, credits, placements, internships... Just come with curiosity and an attitude to learn. The rest, we will figure out together.” Acknowledging that the transition can be particularly challenging for outstation students, LSR offers on-campus counselling support. “At LSR, we have a full-time counsellor, a peer support program in which 10 students are trained to offer psychological first aid to other students under the supervision of the department of Psychology,” Prof Ahuja shares.Prof. Susan Elias, principal of St. Stephen's College notes the importance of the first day, "The first day of college is a memory that will stay with students for years. The first glimpse of the campus, the first class, the first teacher, the first friend, and perhaps the first senior who offers guidance, these moments often shape their sense of belonging. They should spproach the day with curiosity, optimism, and an open mind. Our teaching is rigorous, but it is also supportive, inclusive, and responsive to the realities of the Gen Z and AI era."
Article Summary: New academic session at Delhi University is set to start. freshers are preparing to step onto campus for the very first time. We asked seniors, societies and principals to share what freshers can expect – and how to make the most of their first day.

Article Title: 165 cameras and a race against Coastal Road fire in Mumbai
Article Text:
Coastal road command centre





MUMBAI: At 12.08pm on July 15, an alert flashed across the 30x6-ft video wall inside the Coastal Road's Integrated Command and Control Centre (ICCC) at Breach Candy.A car had caught fire inside the southbound tunnel. Within seconds, CCTV cameras zoomed in on the vehicle, the tunnel's Linear Heat Detection System confirmed a rise in temperature, and an emergency call from a tunnel call box reached the control room.For the team manning the nerve centre of the Coastal Road, it was the biggest emergency since ICCC became operational in Oct 2025. The fire was brought under control without any casualties. But the incident exposed an equally important challenge, managing panic among motorists trapped in a confined underground space.TOI visited ICCC, located at the edge of the Coastal Road interchange at Breach Candy. The facility integrates traffic management, tunnel ventilation, firefighting, surveillance, and mechanical and electrical systems on a single platform.While Coastal Road has separate technical buildings housing equipment, ICCC serves as the central command point for monitoring and controlling the entire corridor, including the twin tunnels."The centre is staffed round the clock by more than 100 personnel working in shifts. Representatives from police, traffic police, fire services and other emergency agencies are also stationed here to ensure coordinated decision-making," said a BMC official.Unlike a conventional CCTV control room, ICCC continuously monitors thousands of data points generated by the tunnel's critical infrastructure. Officials said the system has two key components: the Traffic Management Control System (TMCS), which oversees CCTV cameras, variable message signs and incident detection, and the Plant Management Control System (PMCS), which monitors electrical, mechanical, ventilation and firefighting systems.A key safety feature is the Linear Heat Detection System -- a temperature-sensitive optical cable running through the tunnel that keeps monitoring heat levels and automatically triggers an alarm if temperatures cross about 60 degrees Celsius."The moment the system detects abnormal temperatures, an alert appears on the control room screens. Operators verify it through CCTV feeds and activate the emergency response protocol," said an official from L&T, the EPC contractor for the tunnel package that designed and built much of the tunnel infra and MEP systems.The tunnel is equipped with an Automatic Incident Detection System that analyses live camera feeds to detect stopped vehicles, wrong-way driving, pedestrians and unattended objects. "Once the fire alert was confirmed, the control room activated multiple systems. Public announcements were made in Marathi, Hindi and English, asking motorists to be calm, leave vehicles if necessary and go to the nearest cross-passage. The tunnel's Saccardo ventilation system -- comprising three reversible axial fans -- switched into emergency mode to extract smoke from the affected section," said an official from Tap Turbo Engineers, operations and maintenance contractor for Coastal Road's mechanical and engineering systems.Officials said that under normal conditions, two of the three fans operate at around 70% capacity to maintain air quality. During a fire, the system automatically determines the direction in which smoke should be extracted and, if required, reverses the fans to push smoke away from evacuation routes. "Our priority is not only to extinguish the fire but to remove smoke quickly because smoke poses the biggest risk to human life inside tunnels," an engineer at ICCC said.Officials said the biggest challenge during the incident was not equipment failure but human behaviour. Several motorists ignored repeated announcements to keep the emergency lane clear. Some abandoned their vehicles while others tried to reverse, blocking the route meant for fire engines and rescue vehicles. "Our systems worked exactly as designed. The delay occurred because rescue vehicles could not move freely due to panic among motorists," said M Swami, chief engineer, Coastal Road.The incident prompted authorities to step up public awareness on tunnel safety. Additional signage on evacuation procedures has been installed, and officials said motorists must understand that saving lives takes precedence over saving vehicles. Drivers should switch off the engine, leave the key inside if instructed, evacuate through the nearest emergency exit and avoid reversing or making U-turns in the tunnel. "The systems can manage the fire. What they cannot manage is panic," an official said.
Article Summary: Coastal Road's Integrated Command and Control Centre is located at Breach Candy. The centre is staffed round the clock by more than 100 personnel working in shifts. The facility integrates traffic management, tunnel ventilation, firefighting, surveillance, and mechanical and electrical systems on a single platform.

Article Title: App to store data on deep-sea fishes
Article Text:
Kochi:





ICAR-Central Marine Fisheries Research Institute (ICAR-CMFRI) has recently launched DeepDATA, a mobile application that enables users to explore scientifically verified information on deep-sea fish species and contribute field observations to build a national digital repository. The app is currently available on Google Play Store Students, researchers, fishermen and anyone interested in India’s deep-sea resources can browse photographs and access information on deep-sea fish species, including their taxonomy, distinguishing characteristics, distribution and conservation status. It serves as a digital learning platform for those interested in exploring India’s rich and largely unexplored deep-sea biodiversity.The app was developed under Deep Ocean Mission project with funding from ministry of earth sciences.Designed to encourage citizen participation, the app enables users to upload photographs and observations of deep-sea fishes encountered during fishing operations, research cruises or coastal visits. Every species record uploaded to the platform is verified by CMFRI experts before being added to the database, ensuring scientific accuracy and authenticity.Following scientific validation, these records will generate valuable information on availability and distribution of species in Indian waters.According to Eldho Varghese, in-charge of CMFRI IT unit and lead developer of the app, DeepDATA brings together scientific knowledge and observations from field on a single digital platform, making information on India’s deep-sea biodiversity more accessible while strengthening efforts to document country’s largely unexplored marine resources.
Article Summary: ICAR-Central Marine Fisheries Research Institute has recently launched DeepDATA. The app enables users to upload photographs and observations of deep-sea fishes encountered during fishing operations, research cruises or coastal visits. Every species record uploaded to the platform is verified by CMFRI experts before being added to the database.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Michael Faraday: 'There's nothing quite as frightening as someone who knows they are right' and how blind certainty is human nature's most dangerous trap
Article Text:
'There's nothing quite as frightening as someone who knows they are right'

"There's nothing quite as frightening as someone who knows they are right,

The self-taught genius who questioned everything

The psychological trap of total conviction

Unyielding mindsets in everyday life

The virtue of staying open

A room full of clever people falls silent when someone speaks with total confidence. Doubt creates space for discussion, compromise, and checking the facts. Absolute certainty does the exact opposite. It shuts down debate, ignores warning signs, and treats any disagreement as a personal attack." warned the 19th-century scientist Michael Faraday.Faraday's observation cuts straight to a basic truth about human nature. The quote reminds us that total self-righteousness is far more dangerous than simple ignorance. Someone who knows they do not have all the answers will stop to look at new evidence. Someone who believes they hold the absolute truth feels no need to listen, check facts, or hold back.The origins of this quote belong to a scientist who spent his life fighting against easy assumptions. Born in 1791 to a poor blacksmith in London, Michael Faraday received very little basic schooling. He learned science while working as a bookbinder's apprentice, reading the pages he was hired to stitch together.Through hard work, he earned a job as an assistant to chemist Humphry Davy at the Royal Institution.Faraday went on to discover electromagnetic induction, invent the basic electric motor, and discover benzene.Despite his massive success in physics and chemistry, Faraday remained humble about human knowledge. He was a devoted member of the Sandemanian church, a small Christian group that emphasized humility and the limits of human wisdom. In his science talks during the 1840s and 1850s, Faraday often warned other researchers not to fall in love with their own ideas.While the exact words appear across different letters, journals, and accounts of his talks, Faraday regularly shared this main point: the most dangerous mind in a laboratory is one that has stopped doubting itself.Philosophers and psychologists have long studied why fixed certainty causes so much damage. In the 1990s, psychologists David Dunning and Justin Kruger published landmark research on human thinking, showing that people with limited knowledge in a subject often overestimate their own skill. This phenomenon, known as the Dunning-Kruger effect, shows that confidence often peaks before real understanding even begins.From a philosophical view, Faraday’s warning matches the ideas of Karl Popper, a 20th-century thinker. Popper argued that real science depends on testing ideas to see if they can be proven wrong. A real scientific theory must always stay open to new facts.When a person loses the ability to accept that they might be mistaken, they stop using reason and start following blind belief. History shows that when absolute certainty combines with political, religious, or ideological power, the results are usually terrible. Strict regimes, historical trials, and sudden financial crashes all rely on leaders who are completely convinced of their own correctness.Today, Faraday's warning applies far beyond science labs. Modern digital platforms are built on tools that reward anger and extreme views over thoughtful debate. Online spaces often act as echo chambers, surrounding people with opinions that only confirm what they already believe.This creates leaders, managers, and public figures who refuse to change their minds when conditions shift. In business, major company failures usually trace back to bosses who were completely sure of their plans, ignoring early warnings and feedback from their workers. In health care, government policy, and personal life, a complete refusal to admit doubt stops learning and cuts off teamwork.In contrast, healthy teams depend on what modern workplace psychologists call psychological safety and intellectual humility. Groups perform much better when people can openly say "I do not know" or "I was wrong."Michael Faraday’s entire career succeeded because he refused to believe that existing science had found all the answers. When top scientists believed electricity and magnetism were completely separate, Faraday stayed curious, ran hundreds of failed experiments, and finally proved they were connected.Shortly before his death in 1867, Faraday wrote a letter about his desire to keep his mind free of rigid bias. He understood that knowledge is not a fixed wall, but an ongoing process of testing ideas against real-world facts.Holding onto a healthy sense of doubt is not a sign of weakness. It is a necessary tool for survival, keeping people open to new facts, better ideas, and the simple truth that none of us know everything.
Article Summary: Michael Faraday discovered electromagnetic induction, invent the basic electric motor, and discover benzene. Faraday’s entire career succeeded because he refused to believe that existing science had found all the answers. A real scientific theory must always stay open to new facts.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Slavoj Žižek: 'The problem for us is not are our desires satisfied or not. The problem is...' and the reason why getting everything you want still leaves you feeling completely emp
Article Text:
'The problem for us is not are our desires satisfied or not. The problem is...'

“The problem for us is not are our desires satisfied or not. The problem is how do we know what we desire.”

A scene in a deserted cinema

The Pervert's Guide to Cinema

The problem of borrowed wants

Feeds, apps, and modern choices

You add three items to your online shopping cart, check out, and close the tab. Ten minutes later, you open your phone and start looking at something else. You got what you bought, but the excitement faded before the package even left the warehouse.That strange feeling between getting what you wanted and feeling empty shows a deeper problem: we often do not know what we actually want.As the Slovenian philosopher Slavoj Žižek put it:The quote points out how human unhappiness works today. We usually think suffering comes from missing basic needs like food, money, or freedom.Žižek argues that modern life creates a different kind of frustration. When society gives us endless choices, our main struggle is no longer getting what we ask for, but figuring out whether those wishes are really ours or were handed to us by someone else.This idea appears right at the start of, a 2006 documentary film made by director Sophie Fiennes. In the movie, Žižek stands in a desert, speaking directly to the camera from inside rebuilt movie sets to explain how films shape our minds.In the opening scene, Žižek looks at David Lynch’s 1986 film Blue Velvet and Alfred Hitchcock’s 1954 thriller Rear Window. He argues that movies do not just tell us stories; they act like machines that teach us what to dream about.Instead of seeing movies as a simple escape from real life, Žižek used the film to show that human wishes are mostly built by the world around us. We do not pick our goals out of nowhere. We rely on culture, art, media, and society to give us a model of what is worth chasing.To understand Žižek’s point, it helps to look at French thinker Jacques Lacan, whose ideas heavily influenced Žižek. Lacan wrote that human desire is always shaped by other people.In simple terms, children are not born knowing what to aim for. They watch their parents, friends, and society, and then copy what those people care about. Over time, people mistake these copied goals for their own personal choices.This creates a clear trap. When you finally reach a long-held goal, like buying a specific car or getting a high-status job title, the victory can feel surprisingly flat. That disappointment happens because you achieved someone else’s dream instead of your own.René Girard, a French historian, called this pattern mimetic desire. Girard showed through classic books that people rarely want an object just for what it is. Instead, we want things because we see someone else wanting them. The object becomes a way to get attention or fit in.When Žižek says our real problem is knowing what we want, he is showing how hard it is to separate our true personal goals from what everyone else is doing.This struggle has become much harder in a world run by automated phone apps and smart online feeds.Platforms like TikTok, Instagram, and Spotify do not just guess what you like based on your past clicks. They actively train your tastes. When an app constantly shows short video clips of a certain style, travel spot, or lifestyle, it creates new cravings that feel natural to you.Modern advertising is designed around this exact trick. The goal is no longer just selling a product that fixes a real problem. The goal is making you feel incomplete until you buy it.When you buy something recommended by a feed, you satisfy a need that the phone created just minutes earlier. You feel in control, but your decision was guided from the outside.This same pattern shows up at work. Many people experience burnout because they spend years grinding for a big promotion or a prestigious title, only to realize when they get it that they never enjoyed the actual work. They wanted the status that came with the job, not the daily job itself.Fixing this confusion starts with realizing that our first instincts are rarely original. Figure out where your choices come from, because chasing the wrong goal means gaining nothing when you finally catch it.
Article Summary: Slavoj Žižek argues that modern life creates a different kind of frustration. When society gives us endless choices, our main struggle is not getting what we ask for, but figuring out whether those wishes are really ours or were handed to us by someone else.

Article Title: A UK village spent £35,000 building four beaver-style dams after homes flooded. It is now waiting for the next deluge during a hosepipe ban
Article Text:
Leaky dams, also known as logjams, allow water to flow through slowly instead of blocking it. (Representational AI image)

Customers have been asked to avoid using hosepipes for watering gardens, washing cars, and filling paddling pools or hot tubs. (Representational AI photo)

From drought to floods

Beavers are called ecosystem engineers because they naturally reshape rivers and wetlands by building dams.

Learning from Beavers

East Anglia, a rural region in eastern England, is facing a hosepipe ban after becoming the driest part of the UK. But in one village in Norfolk, people are also preparing for the opposite problem of flooding.At Caistor St Edmund, the ground has become so dry and hard that it feels like walking on a paved road. Farmers have harvested this year's hay, but the crop is smaller than usual. If rain does not arrive soon, they fear there may not be a second harvest.The long spell of hot, dry weather has forced Anglian Water, a water recycling company, to bring in its first hosepipe ban in 10 years. People have been asked not to use hosepipes for watering gardens, washing cars or filling paddling pools and hot tubs. However, they can still use watering cans.East Anglia is the driest region in the UK. According to Anglian Water, the area received only 39% of its normal rainfall this spring, making it the second driest spring on record. Many rivers are running at very low levels, reservoirs have less water than usual, and record-breaking temperatures have increased water use."Understandably, customers have wanted to stay cool and have fun in the sun, but the unrelenting conditions are placing the environment and water supplies under increasing strain," said Dr Geoff Darch, Anglian Water's head of strategic asset planning, as quoted by the BBC.He urged people to "hang up the hosepipe, let lawns go brown, cars go dirty and use water even more wisely".Today, people are being asked to save every drop of water. But residents of Caistor St Edmund have not forgotten what happened when there was too much of it.According to The Guardian, the dry weather is very different from what the village experienced in December 2020. Days of heavy rain overwhelmed drains as water rushed off nearby fields. Roads turned into fast-moving streams of muddy water, homes flooded despite sandbags, and volunteers worked to keep drains clear. Residents say it was the worst flooding they had seen.To reduce the risk of another flood, four wooden structures have now been built along Wash Lane, where the watercourse is currently dry. These structures are called leaky dams or logjams. They do not block the water completely, but slows it down. During heavy rain, they also trap branches and other natural materials, helping slow the flow before the water reaches roads and homes.Norfolk County Council has spent more than £35,000 on the project. The idea is inspired by beavers, often called ecosystem engineers because they naturally reshape rivers and wetlands by building dams.When beavers cut down trees and build dams, they slow the movement of water and create small ponds. These ponds also become breeding sites for wildlife such as dragonflies and amphibians, including frogs, toads and newts.Norfolk has a small number of released beavers, and some have bred successfully, but none live near this village. The wooden leaky dams are designed to copy the way beaver dams work and provide similar flood-control benefits.The project reflects a growing need to prepare for more extreme weather, with long dry spells followed by periods of heavy rain. While the leaky dams are expected to reduce flood risk, there are also plans for a large solar development in nearby fields. This could change rainwater runoff, the way rainwater moves across the ground before reaching streams and drains.
Article Summary: East Anglia, a rural region in eastern England, is facing a hosepipe ban after becoming the driest part of the UK. People have been asked not to use hosepipes for watering gardens, washing cars or filling paddling pools or hot tubs. But in one village in Norfolk, people are also preparing for the opposite problem of flooding.

Article Title: In 2022, New York prospectors searched Diamond District sidewalk cracks for traces of gold, platinum and gemstones; some claimed earnings of $300 a day
Article Text:
Prospectors in New York's Diamond District searched sidewalk cracks for valuable materials. They used brushes and vacuums to collect dust and debris from pavements. Image Credit: Wikimedia Commons

What are the methods of

sidewalk prospecting

?

Why do valuables end up on the sidewalk?

This residue, known as paydirt, contained traces of gold and diamonds. Valuables ended up on the sidewalk due to extensive jewelry trading and repair activities. Image Credit: Wikimedia Commons

Gold extraction science from soil

Urban treasure hunters beyond New York

The Diamond District of New York City is recognised across the world for its jewellery shops, diamond dealers and gemstone markets. However, in 2022, there were some prospectors who, instead of looking at the shining shops, focused on an unexpected location: the cracks in the sidewalk.Using brushes, hooks, buckets and portable vacuum cleaners, the prospectors sifted dust and debris from pavements in and around the Manhattan jewellery district to recover traces of gold, platinum, diamonds and gemstones left behind by years of trading and jewellery repair. According to the International Gemological Institute , some street prospectors say they can earn hundreds of dollars a day, with some reporting earnings of about $300It entails collecting a mixed composition of soil, dust, metal shards, and other residues found in pavements' cracks and later separating them to search for any valuable contents. From reports on New York sidewalk prospecting, one example is Klesh, who began prospecting around the Diamond District at the corner of Fifth Avenue and West 47th Street.He uses a steel hook pick, brush, and vacuum to gather residues in pavement cracks and separates them to find heavy metals or gemstone shards. The residues collected through sidewalk prospecting are called "paydirt," a mining term for material that contains valuable mineral deposits.The Diamond District is one of the world’s best-known jewellery-trading areas. It includes hundreds of jewellery shops situated around West 47th Street, Fifth and Sixth Avenue in Manhattan, and it specializes in the trade of diamonds, gems, and precious metals.Because buying, selling, repairing and processing jewellery happen in such a compact area, small traces of valuable material can sometimes end up in street dust. Identification of the materials, however, is not always easy. According to the Gemological Institute of America (GIA), it is often hard to identify what kind of stone you have - a natural diamond, laboratory-made diamond, or a fake one. According to GIA, some special devices are often needed because sometimes diamonds cannot be recognised by just looking at them.There are many scientific concepts behind the extraction of metals from the soil, including gold extraction science. Gold is an element that has high density, making it possible to use its properties for separation using gravity separation techniques.According to the US Geological Survey , the dense nature and stability of gold cause it to deposit in certain places, and hence, it can be separated using gravity separation techniques from other materials of lower density. Street prospectors use the same principle but on a much smaller scale in order to find dense material from soil deposits.The hunt for useful and valuable items in urban settings does not stop at New York alone. Metal detecting, recycling and urban scavenging are practiced by people all around the globe in their search for useful and valuable objects.The distinctive feature of this activity is that ordinary urban dust may contain material linked to jewellery making. Although searching for diamonds and gold in the sidewalk cracks may seem like a treasure hunt, valuable materials are not so easy to recover.It takes patience, skill, and the capacity to find any valuable material amid the tons of waste. The Diamond District hunters' tale shows one of the peculiarities of city living, as amid millions of footprints and layers of urban dust, some valuable items may still remain unnoticed.
Article Summary: Prospectors in New York's Diamond District searched sidewalk cracks for valuable materials. They used brushes and vacuums to collect dust and debris from pavements. This residue, known as paydirt, contained traces of gold and diamonds. Valuables ended up on the sidewalk due to extensive jewelry trading and repair activities.

Article Title: America is committing trillions to rebuild. AI must help people build it
Article Text:
AI is useful, but only when it is grounded in the judgment of people

I have spent more than two decades building AI systems, and I am also a father of two young children. These two facts shape how I think about the future we are building. When AI companies claim they are building systems to replace people, I believe them. I know what this powerful technology can do, but as a parent, I worry about what we choose to do with it.The United States is entering a period of reindustrialization. Roughly $2 trillion is flowing into manufacturing, infrastructure, energy, semiconductors, and the industries that will define the future. But the people needed to build it are in short supply.What we build with AI, and who benefits from it, is still our choice.The numbers make the stakes plain. Manufacturing alone could face 2.1 million unfilled jobs by 2030, a shortage that could cost the U.S. economy up to $1 trillion that year. The construction and skilled trades sector is short more than 530,000 workers in 2026 alone. Aviation faces a projected shortage of 60,000 maintenance technicians by 2029 if the pipeline does not improve. And even as AI displaces some work in other sectors, 170 million new roles are projected to be created by 2030, roles that will require exactly the kind of skilled, experienced people we are struggling to find.The challenge isn’t simply finding more workers. It is helping people across the workforce build, share, and keep improving the know-how this moment demands. We do not have a shortage of know-how in this country, but every retirement takes decades of hard-earned know-how with it. For every five skilled workers who retire, only two enter the trades. That is the gap we should be asking AI to close.So, the question is not whether AI changes work. It will.The real question is whether we use AI to replace know-how or multiply it.Know-how earned from decades of work is different from written information. It is what people learn after years of doing real work: what to notice, when to slow down, when to escalate, when something feels off, and how to solve a problem that does not look like the textbook or the checklist.Think about a 22-year-old aviation safety mechanic on the first day of the job. Then comes a vibration, a temperature change, something that does not match what the manuals describe. An experienced mechanic may have seen that pattern before. They know when to slow down, when to escalate, and how to diagnose the problem.This need for experienced, embodied knowledge repeats across industries. An electrician wiring a new manufacturing plant. The construction supervisor who spots a problem before it becomes an accident. The manufacturing engineer who knows why a production line keeps failing. A nurse who notices a patient declining before the chart makes it obvious. The physician whose judgment helps treat complex cases. The small business owner who spent decades earning trust, training people, and learning how to serve a community.When that hard-earned know-how walks out the door, we all lose.Ford learned this the hard way. After three years of quality problems, the company turned back to about 350 veteran engineers and technical specialists to mentor younger workers, lead design reviews, and improve the AI tools used to catch defects earlier. Ford’s lesson was clear: AI is useful, but only when it is grounded in the judgment of people who know the work. Their expertise was not the cost to cut. It was the competitive advantage Ford could not afford to lose.Ford is not alone. Research shows that more than a third of companies that conducted AI-driven layoffs had to rehire more than half the workers they let go.Too much of today’s AI is designed to keep people coming back for answers, not to help them build lasting know-how. That is the same mistake social media made: engagement over agency. AI should not become another technology that takes human agency away. It should help people become more capable, not more dependent.What we need is AI that works alongside experienced people, continually learning from the decisions they make and the problems they solve, and helps bring the next person up to speed faster. In some roles, that could compress expertise that once took years to build into weeks or months of guided learning.That is one reason we started Cognisee: to build AI that learns with how people think, judge, and act, and puts that hard-earned judgment within reach of every person who comes after them, so we never have to choose between experience and scale.Building takes more than capital. It takes people who know how to build, fix, operate, and improve the systems our country depends on. And it takes making sure their know-how multiplies, not disappears.The promised age of abundance cannot be built by leaving people behind.The true measure of AI is not how much work it takes away from people. It is how much value it helps us create for families, businesses, communities, and nations.Because the future will not be built by AI alone. It will be built by people whose knowledge, judgment, and purpose are multiplied by it.

Difference between a Nominee and a Legal heir

Aspect Nominee Legal Heir Role Custodian Owner Transfer of Assets Can be done without any legal formalities. Requires testamentary documents for proof of ownership. Powers No power to transact, use, or transfer assets. Power to use and transact assets as an owner. Appointment Owner can appoint anyone, but some institutions specify certain conditions. Determined by succession/personal laws. Legal Right Cannot contest ownership legally. Can contest ownership in a court of law.

When individuals open bank accounts, invest in mutual funds, or buy insurance, they are often asked to name a nominee.However, many people mistakenly assume that the nominee automatically inherits the assets. In reality, the nominee is not always the final recipient — the ownership rights belong to the legal heir, reported ET.Understanding the distinction between these two is essential to ensure that your wealth is passed on to the intended beneficiaries.A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets.The nominee’s role is limited to holding and managing the assets until they are legally transferred to the rightful heirs.According to ET, the nominee cannot sell, trade, or make any transactional decisions about the assets.The account or policy owner can appoint anyone — family, friends, or acquaintances — as a nominee, though financial institutions often prefer close family members.In some cases, the nominee and the legal heir can be the same person, which helps in ensuring a smoother transfer of assets.The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away.To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will or other testamentary proof.If there is no will — a situation known as dying intestate — the heir is determined as per the country’s succession or personal laws, reported ET.While a nominee can initially access the assets, only the legal heir can claim them permanently or challenge ownership in court.Experts quoted by ET emphasise that having clarity on this difference helps avoid disputes and ensures that the savings reach the intended family members or beneficiaries.Therefore, it is advisable to regularly update both nominees and wills to align with one’s estate planning goals.

How Jeevan Pramaan simplifies pensioner verification



Every year, lakhs of pensioners across India must prove that they are still alive to continue receiving their pension. This verification, known as the Life Certificate or Digital Life Certificate (DLC), is a crucial and mandatory step in ensuring that pension payments are made only to eligible recipients, preventing fraud and misuse.Traditionally, this process involved visiting the bank or pension office in person, standing in long queues, and submitting a signed paper certificate. However, with the government’s focus on digitisation and technological advancement, this process has become much simpler, faster, and more convenient. Pensioners can now submit their certificates digitally from the comfort of their homes using Jeevan Pramaan, a secure, user-friendly, and Aadhaar-based platform.A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries.The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric-enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.Introduced by the Government of India, it uses Aadhaar-based biometric authentication using either fingerprint or iris scan to verify a pensioner’s identity. Once verified, a digital certificate is automatically generated and shared with authorised pension disbursing agencies.This online process eliminates the need for physical verification, providing elderly pensioners with a simpler and more accessible way to maintain their pension benefits.According to PIB, The submission of the Life Certificate is mandatory for all pensioners who wish to continue receiving their pension without interruption. For the year 2025, the standard submission period is betweenTo make the process more comfortable for the elderly, the government allows pensioners aged 80 years and above to begin the submission process earlier, from 1 October 2025. This extended window gives senior citizens more time and flexibility to complete the procedure without facing last-minute difficulties.The Jeevan Pramaan process involves two main steps: registering the biometric device and generating the digital certificate.Before using the service, pensioners or operators must register their biometric device such as a fingerprint or iris scanner. During registration, the user provides their Aadhaar number and mobile number, after which an OTP (One-Time Password) is sent to their mobile. After entering the OTP, they must provide their name and email ID before scanning their fingerprint or iris.Once authentication is complete, the system confirms that device registration was successful, allowing the user to move to the next step.In this step, the pensioner enters personal details such as Aadhaar number, mobile number, name, PPO number, pension type, sanctioning authority, disbursing agency, and bank account details. The system also asks whether the pensioner has remarried or is re-employed.After entering all details, the pensioner scans their fingerprint or iris using the registered biometric device. Upon successful authentication, the Digital Life Certificate is generated, and an SMS acknowledgment with the Jeevan Pramaan Certificate ID is sent to the registered mobile number.This certificate is automatically stored in the Life Certificate Repository, accessible anytime to both pensioners and pension agencies.Once the Digital Life Certificate is created, it can be electronically delivered to the concerned Pension Disbursing Agency (PDA). PDAs can log in to the Jeevan Pramaan portal to view, verify, or download the certificate directly.Pensioners can also download a PDF copy of their certificate by visiting the Jeevan Pramaan website and entering their Pramaan ID or Aadhaar number. This ensures transparency and easy access for future reference.The government provides several options to submit the Life Certificate, allowing pensioners to choose the method that suits them best.Pensioners who prefer traditional methods can visit their bank branch or a Citizen Service Centre (CSC) to submit their Life Certificate physically. Trained staff at these centres assist pensioners in verifying their details and completing the process.For those unable to travel due to age or health issues, India Post Payments Bank (IPPB) offers a doorstep banking service. Pensioners can schedule an appointment, and an IPPB representative will visit their home to complete the submission using biometric authentication. This service is available for both IPPB and non-IPPB account holders.For pensioners comfortable with technology, the Jeevan Pramaan portal provides a completely online process. By visiting https://jeevanpramaan.gov.in, pensioners can submit their Digital Life Certificate using a computer, laptop, or smartphone equipped with a fingerprint or iris scanner.The system uses the Aadhaar platform to authenticate biometric details. Once verification is successful, a Digital Life Certificate is generated and stored in a secure online repository. Pension disbursing agencies can then directly access the certificate, removing the need for physical paperwork.The UMANG (Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance) app offers another easy option. Pensioners can download the app from the Google Play Store, search for “Jeevan Pramaan,” and select “Generate Life Certificate.”After entering the necessary details such as Aadhaar number, PPO number, and type of pension, pensioners must authenticate themselves using biometric verification. The app then generates a Digital Life Certificate (DLC), which is automatically shared with the pension disbursing authority.All pensioners who receive government, defence, or private sector pensions through authorised disbursing agencies are required to submit their Life Certificate every year. This includes:Failure to submit the certificate within the stipulated period may result in temporary suspension of pension payments until verification is completed.To ensure a smooth submission process, pensioners should keep certain details and documents ready. These include:Having these details ready helps to avoid delays or errors during authentication, whether submitting online or offline.Yes, an Aadhaar number or Virtual ID (VID) is mandatory to generate a Digital Life Certificate. The entire Jeevan Pramaan system is based on Aadhaar authentication, which ensures accuracy and prevents fraud. Pensioners must make sure their Aadhaar is linked with their mobile number and bank account before attempting to generate the certificate.The Digital Life Certificate is fully valid and legally recognised under the Information Technology Act. Pension disbursing authorities across India accept it as an official document, equivalent to the traditional paper-based life certificate.Its biometric verification system makes it secure and tamper-proof, reducing the chances of wrongful pension disbursal or misuse of pension funds.Before the introduction of Jeevan Pramaan, pensioners often faced difficulties in submitting their certificates, especially those with health problems or limited mobility. The digital system has removed these challenges, allowing pensioners to submit their verification anytime and anywhere.By integrating biometric technology and Aadhaar authentication, Jeevan Pramaan has streamlined pension management, improving efficiency for both pensioners and government departments. It also enhances transparency and ensures that genuine beneficiaries receive payments on time.
Article Summary: A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries. The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric- enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.

Article Title: Read letter that has Satya Nadella, Sundar Pichai, Elon Musk, Jensen Huang, Sam Altman and many other CEOs of biggest American technology companies saying: 'This has our full support'
Article Text:
Arguments for openness

Access : Startups and universities can build on advanced models without prohibitive costs.

: Startups and universities can build on advanced models without prohibitive costs. Competition : Rivalry across developers, chips, and services drives innovation and lowers costs.

: Rivalry across developers, chips, and services drives innovation and lowers costs. Control : Organizations avoid lock-in and retain ownership of their AI capabilities.

: Organizations avoid lock-in and retain ownership of their AI capabilities. Security: Transparency allows vulnerabilities to be identified and remediated across many teams.

Read the letter here

Open Weights and American AI Leadership

July 24, 2026

In the 1980s, early open-source software pioneers challenged the prevailing belief that software would advance only if companies kept tight control over their code. This movement pushed for a transparent ecosystem where developers around the world could study, modify, and improve software. Software developed by the open-source community now supports most of the internet and underlies systems used by the world’s largest technology companies, as well as the U.S. military and federal agencies conducting scientific research, cybersecurity, and other critical missions. Open source did more than lower the cost of software; it created a shared foundation of knowledge on which generations of American engineers and entrepreneurs built their institutional sovereignty.

The United States now faces a similar choice with artificial intelligence. Our AI leadership will be judged not by one frontier AI model, but by whether the United States builds a strong, open ecosystem that diffuses into every sector. This is essential for creating opportunities for innovation and prosperity across the country. It requires expanding access to AI, encouraging competition, robust application layers, and giving Americans greater control over the technology they rely on. Open weight models—AI models that anyone can download, inspect, modify, and run on their own infrastructure—are an important part of that foundation because they make advanced AI more accessible, adaptable, and widely available.

Open weights expand access to the AI economy. Startups, established businesses, universities, and public institutions can build on advanced models without training one from scratch or paying frontier-model prices for every task. Open weights let every organization match the right model to the right job at the right cost, reserving frontier-scale capability for genuine frontier problems and running efficient, specialized models everywhere else. That discipline is what will make AI economically sustainable as its use scales into the billions of everyday tasks. America wins the AI era by diffusing it into the workflows of factories, hospitals, farms, classrooms, and main street businesses.

Open weights also strengthen competition and competition is what keeps the gains of AI broadly shared rather than concentrated in a few hands. By allowing many organizations to build, adapt, and deploy advanced models, open weights create rivalry not only among model developers but across cloud chips, applications, and services. That competition spurs innovation, drives down costs, and distributes the benefits of AI broadly across our economy.

Open weights also give customers greater control. As organizations invest in AI, they want to know that they will not become locked into a single provider or lose the knowledge and capabilities they build over time. Open weight models help provide that assurance by allowing organizations to control their own data, evaluate and adapt models to their own needs, and deploy them wherever their business requirements demand. And as organizations create value with AI, open weights allow them to own that value through self-improving models, specialized capabilities, and accumulated knowledge that drive American sovereignty and prosperity.

To be sure, open weights carry real and distinct risks. Once released, the weights are beyond the original developer’s control, and modified versions are difficult to trace or reverse. But the right response to this risk is not to prohibit open weights. In a world where cybersecurity attackers use advanced AI, defenders need access to models with comparable capabilities so they can detect, simulate, and respond to emerging threats. Open models broaden defensive capability, increase transparency, and allow vulnerabilities to be discovered and remediated across many teams.

In fact, openness may be one of the most important paths to AI safety and security. Relying solely on closed models is not inherently safe: they can be breached, misused, or fail in ways that outsiders cannot detect. And concentrating advanced AI capabilities behind a small number of closed models compounds that risk. It results in a small number of single points of failure, weakens competition, and leaves critical technology in the hands of a few providers. Open weight models, on the other hand, allow a broad community of researchers and developers to examine their behavior, identify vulnerabilities, develop safeguards, and improve them over time. Just as open-source software demonstrated that transparency can be more secure than obscurity, AI safety may depend on giving more people the ability to test and strengthen the models on which society relies. It allows for rigorous benchmarking and evaluation, red teaming, and protections tied to real and demonstrated harms rather than assuming that closed systems are safer by default.

A strong AI ecosystem is not a foregone conclusion. Policymakers have an important opportunity to act. This includes expanding access to compute for startups and researchers, investing in shared training assets (datasets, tools, evaluation frameworks), and keeping the frontier plural by avoiding premature restrictions on open models that stifle competition or drive innovation overseas. These measures must also look at how strong application layers can expand sovereign use of AI across the economy.

In shaping this ecosystem, policymakers should be careful not to conflate legitimate model-development techniques with misappropriation. Distillation, or the practice of using one model’s outputs to help train or improve another, is a widely used technique for model improvement, evaluation, and validation. It reflects a long tradition of learning from, building upon, and improving existing technologies, a tradition that has helped drive innovation since the rise of the open-source software movement. By contrast, unlawful efforts to extract value from closed models raise legitimate concerns. Those concerns should be addressed through targeted legal and commercial frameworks rather than sweeping restrictions on techniques that play an important role in AI innovation.

The age of AI can be one of prosperity. With the right choices, open weight AI can expand opportunity, strengthen competition, extend American technological leadership, mitigate risk, and ensure that the benefits of this extraordinary technology are shared broadly across our economy. That future is worth building, and the United States should lead in building it.

A coalition of 25 leading technology companies and organisations has published a joint letter titled Open Weights and American AI Leadership recently, is urging policymakers to embrace open-weight AI models. The letter argues that America’s AI leadership depends not on a single frontier model but on building a strong, open ecosystem that diffuses across industries. It highlights how open weights AI models that anyone can download, inspect, and run expand access, spur competition, and give greater control to organisations over their data and capabilities. The letter has also drawn endorsements from the biggest names in technology.Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella wrote, “Open-weight models are essential to a healthy AI ecosystem. Together with others across our industry, we are outlining a path for open-weight models to strengthen American competitiveness and expand economic opportunity, while protecting national security,” supporting the letter on X. Sundar Pichai, CEO of Google, posted, “Very happy to support this on behalf of Google. We have long benefited from open source, are big contributors to open source and in fact have consistently made open weights models with Gemma available from @GoogleDeepMind @demishassabis .Onwards!”OpenAI’s Sam Altman also endorsed the letter and wrote on X, “i want the US to win in AI both in open source and proprietary models, and i am glad to see this.” “This has my full support,” added Elon Musk . Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang joined the chorus, highlighting the importance of open-weight AI for startups, researchers, and public institutions and posted on X, “For my first post, I’m sharing a letter @NVIDIA signed on why open models matter. AI will transform every industry, power every company, and be built by every country. Open models strengthen safety and cybersecurity, accelerate innovation and diffusion, and enable sovereignty. The world needs both frontier closed models and frontier open models.”The coalition’s letter outlines several benefits of open weights:
Article Summary: Open Weights and American AI Leadership will be judged by whether the U.S. builds a strong, open ecosystem that diffuses into every sector. It requires expanding access to AI, encouraging competition, robust application layers, and giving Americans greater control over technology they rely on.

Article Title: New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani is hiring software engineers, designers, researchers for his 'tech crew': Here's what the job actually is
Article Text:
NYC mayor wants his ‘tech crew’ to build city software from inside the agency



New York City is betting that in-house tech teams will ship faster and cost less



New York City has opened applications for a new kind of government job. Mayor Zohran Mamdani announced on Monday that the city is recruiting software engineers, product designers, product managers, user researchers, service designers and data experts to staff what he is calling Public Interest Technology Crews—PIT Crews, a pun the mayor committed to by rolling up to the Coney Island go-kart track to make the announcement.The hiring is funded and specific. A City Hall spokesperson confirmed around 30 full-time roles across four crews, supported by $5.24 million in baseline funding in the mayor's new fiscal budget. The listings are live at nyc.gov/pitcrew.A PIT Crew is a mixed team—engineers, designers, product managers, user researchers and data experts—placed alongside staff at a city agency rather than parked in a separate technology department. The crew works with that agency and with New Yorkers to design, build and launch a digital tool, then learn from how people actually use it. The mayor's office describes the timeline as months rather than years, which is the entire premise of the model.Five crews are planned. One handles the Click to Cancel complaint portal, three are attached to Mamdani's affordability and public excellence agenda, and a fifth is being developed with support from The Rockefeller Foundation through the Mayor's Fund to Advance New York City.Zohran Mamdani’s PIT crew’s first assignment is a complaint portal with teethCrew one works with the Department of Consumer and Worker Protection on an online portal where New Yorkers can report companies that make subscriptions near-impossible to cancel. It supports the Click to Cancel rule Mamdani announced last week, which requires businesses to offer the same exit route customers used to sign up. Enforcement begins October 1, and the junk fees ban lands January 1, 2027.The portal is built to do two things at once—give individual New Yorkers a route to recourse, and give City Hall a running database of repeat offenders.Chief Technology Officer and OTI Commissioner Lisa Gelobter framed the roles around a shift in what government technology now is. Every service has a digital surface, she argued, and every confusing step in that surface erodes trust. Her operating instruction for the crews is user first, always, with outcomes weighted over outputs.There is a politics to the hiring as well. NYC-DSA's Tech Action organisers backed the announcement as a choice to build capacity inside government rather than route taxpayer money to consultancies and big tech vendors. BetaNYC's Noel Hidalgo made the cost version of the same argument—in-house teams that deliver faster and cheaper than the outsourced alternative."New Yorkers should not be forced to navigate systems that are confusing, outdated and burdened by bureaucracy," Mamdani said. "The PIT Crew turns that model on its head."Public Interest Technology took shape as a field in the 2010s on a fairly unglamorous premise: government software is usually bad, and fixing it is a staffing and usability problem more than an engineering one. The recruitment page leans into that, pitching the work rather than the salary—the goal, it says, is to make interacting with government dignified and delightful for every New Yorker.
Article Summary: New York City launches Public Interest Technology Crews (PIT Crews) Crews will build city software from inside the agency rather than in a separate department. Hiring is funded by $5.24 million in the mayor's new fiscal budget.

Article Title: YouTube will now help creators make thumbnails easily using AI
Article Text:
Custom thumbnails arrive for YouTube Shorts

YouTube has announced a series of updates that are designed to simplify and speed up the thumbnail creation process, giving creators more control over how their content appears across the platform.
